effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per structural claim of the Bedrock Architecture Overview, in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in logos-blockchain-core or logos-blockchain-ledger that fails on 0.3.0 for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (commit 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is the LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot).

The document is the top-level description of the Bedrock layers (Cryptarchia consensus, the ledger, Mantle operations, the services on top) and of what each layer owns. Its requirements are the responsibilities and boundaries it assigns to each layer, the data each layer holds, and the order in which a block is validated and applied. Detailed protocols are audited by their own briefs; here, trace the structural claims.

Where the structure lives in the code:
- core/src/lib.rs, src/block/ (block, genesis.rs, uncle.rs, deser.rs) and src/header/ (package `logos-blockchain-core`): the block and header types shared by every layer; src/mantle/mod.rs the Mantle transaction type.
- ledger/src/lib.rs (package `logos-blockchain-ledger`): the top-level `Ledger`, its `Config`, `LedgerError`, and the entry point that validates and applies a block; src/update.rs the per-block update; src/mantle/mod.rs the Mantle execution layer; src/cryptarchia/ (outside the unit, read for context) the consensus state.
- nodes/node/binary/src/lib.rs and src/generic_services/ (package `logos-blockchain-node`, not in the gate, read for tracing only): how the node binary wires the services (chain, chain-leader, chain-network, mempool, blend, sdp, pow, wallet, api) together; services/*/src are the services themselves, outside the unit.

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's testable packages with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
